source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.

gens.text: Through the bustling terminal, beyond the barriers, stood a line where everyone’s possessions were laid bare on trays. Each passenger, after passing the scanning machines, was directed to remove items from their person, as an officer watched diligently over a traveler selected for further inspection. The man was instructed to hand over his documents and undergo a pat-down with a handheld device, his compliance marked by the courteous but firm gestures of the official. As he waited, the traveler noted the surrounding signs detailing procedures and regulations, the atmosphere charged yet orderly under the watchful eyes of security. He felt a slight tap on his back as the wand swept across, each beep signaling another check point completed. Beside him, another traveler prepared to join the queue, their belongings spread out on a tray, ready for their turn under scrutiny. Throughout, the officers maintained a professional distance, their interactions brief and to the point. With the pat-down concluded, the traveler retrieved his belongings, feeling a mix of relief and weariness. Nearby, a sign reminded all passengers of the importance of following instructions closely, and the traveler, now through the checkpoint, joined the flow of travelers beyond the barriers, the controlled chaos of the terminal resuming around him. As he moved towards his gate, a final prompt whispered that he should remain vigilant and alert for any announcements, the impersonal courtesy of authority echoing in his mind.

At the entrance beyond, through a lane guarded by partitions, travelers queued, their belongings laid out on conveyors beneath the watchful gaze of X-ray machines and the steady hum of metal detectors. Among them, an officer selected a passenger from the line, motioning to divest further items into a tray. With documents displayed, they were guided towards a private space for closer inspection; an electronic wand traced over clothing, methodical in its scrutiny. The atmosphere was marked by authoritative yet courteous commands, directional signs overhead guiding movements, and the pervasive presence of security personnel maintaining order. Every individual, though anonymized within the process, responded to the standardized protocol, a ritual of compliance enacted under the vigilant eyes of surveillance cameras and officers alike. Through this rigorous yet structured routine, the flow of people moved steadily, each moment encapsulated by the orchestrated precision of security measures designed to ensure public safety. Beyond the checkpoints, announcements echoed, coordinating arrivals and departures, a symphony of directives balancing efficiency with the occasional personal touch—a reminder of the human interaction amidst the regulated environment. In this corridor of control, every step was accounted for, each item scrutinized, embodying the balance between privacy and public duty, where every traveler was treated equally, under the unyielding rule of procedure. As one left this area, the echo of footsteps on tile was replaced by the gentle whoosh of gates opening, signaling the conclusion of an experience that combined impersonal rigidity with the underlying warmth of institutional care, ensuring a safe passage through.
